newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle, feeder cattle futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle, feeder cattle futures end lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower as sagging beef prices weighed down live cattle futures and profit taking pushed feeder cattle lower, traders said.

Hedge selling by feedlot interests was noted in live cattle against a mix of commission house and commercial buying, traders said. Also, in the feeder cattle pit, traders said Cargill was noted buying March feeder cattle and selling June live cattle.
Lower beef prices caused much of the bearishness among cattle traders. And with Lent beginning Feb 12, some traders doubt there will be a significant change in beef demand.

Also, CME traders expected $66.00 per cwt sales in Plains feedlot markets early Wednesday, but feedlot trading was generally quiet through midday, with only a small number of heifers selling in Kansas at $66.50.
However, USDA also reported sales of steers and heifers in Nebraska at a steady $66.00 on a live basis and $107.00 on a carcass basis.
